title: Mitigating Gradient Pathology in PINNs through Aligned Constraint
claim: A simple, well-behaved loss landscape in function space becomes highly distorted and non-convex when mapped through the network into parameter space.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, contour plots, red valley curve overlaid
description: Two side-by-side contour plots of a PDE residual loss landscape, each with a red curve tracing the loss valley. Panel (a), labeled Function Space, shows straight horizontal bands. The colors run from yellow at the top and bottom to dark teal near the middle, and the red valley is a straight horizontal line at y=0. The loss is simple and convex-like. Panel (b), labeled Parameter Space, uses the same viridis-like colormap, but the contours are twisted and winding, with several basins and a flat plateau in the middle. The red valley path bends sharply, zigzags, and follows a narrow curved canyon between local minima. The eye goes first to the red curves. The contrast between the straight line and the winding path carries the argument. Axes are numeric, and the subpanel captions are large serif text.
caption: Visualization of the PDE residual loss landscape in both the function space and the parameter space, projected onto a 2D subspace. The red curve indicates the loss valley. While the landscape is relatively simple in the function space, it becomes highly distorted and non-convex when mapped to the parameter space by the neural network. More details are in Appendix [ref].
abstract: While Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are powerful for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), their training is often paralyzed by gradient pathology. The gradients from the PDE residuals and boundary constraints oppose each other, trapping the model in local minima. Current solutions, such as adaptive weighting or hard constraints, either fail to fundamentally resolve this ill-conditioning or are limited to simple geometries. In this study, we systematically analyze the possible causes of this gradient pathology from the perspectives of loss landscapes and optimization dynamics. Based on the obtained conclusion, we propose Constraint-Aligned loss with Manifold Lifting (CAML). By reformulating all zeroth-order terms into aligned constraints, our method effectively mitigates gradient conflicts. In addition, we introduce a delay factor to help the optimizer skip the high-curvature area. Experiments demonstrate that our CAML significantly enhances numerical stability and efficiency in highly complex PINN problems. Our code is open-sourced on https://github.com/YichenLuo-0/CAML.
